Subject: Payment terms – request for temporary extension and credit increase

Hi Sergio / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick delivery estimate — Shan has pushed this internally and we're ready to move forward. One operational constraint I need to flag from our side: Finance has an incoming cutover to a new AP vendor and our invoice processing times will be longer than usual for the next 60 days.

Given that, could Redwood consider a temporary extension to Net60 for the next two invoices for the pilot? We can sign an amended SOW or a one-page payment addendum to formalize.

If Net60 is not possible, would you accept a split remit where 30% is paid at invoice date (Net30) and the balance at Net60? Alternatively, we could do a milestone schedule (partial at kickoff, remainder on delivery). Also, because we're cross-border: we need VAT‑breakouts on any invoices and confirmation if Redwood can reference the reverse-charge on invoices (we're a UK VAT‑registered business).

Attachments: PO_4571.pdf (our purchase order)

Appreciate any flexibility — Liam

--

Hi Liam — thanks for the context and for sharing PO_4571. Happy to work through a short-term arrangement so we can start the pilot without cashflow surprises on either side.

Proposal (short-term, pilot-specific):
- Amended payment schedule (attached):
  - Invoice 1 (kickoff): 40% due within 30 days of invoice date (Net30)
  - Invoice 2 (delivery milestone): 50% due within 45 days of that invoice date (Net45)
  - Retention: 10% held and due at 60 days after final delivery (Net60)
- This is a temporary cadence for the next two invoices tied to PO_4571. After the pilot, standard terms would revert to Net30 unless we agree otherwise.
- VAT: Redwood can include VAT line items and reference the UK reverse-charge mechanism, but we will need MediFlex's VAT registration number and confirmation of reverse-charge eligibility on your end. If reverse-charge applies, we will issue a VAT-inclusive invoice with a reverse-charge note (no VAT collected).
- Credit: we can temporarily increase the short-term credit ceiling to accommodate the split schedule for the length of the pilot, subject to a brief credit review (1–2 business days).

Next steps: if that works, I'll draft a one-page payment addendum and a revised invoice schedule (xlsx attached). If you prefer a lower kickoff percentage, tell us what works and we'll iterate — our priority is to avoid blocking delivery.

Attachments: proposed_payment_schedule.xlsx

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0192

Marissa — thanks, that proposed split looks workable in principle. Two quick asks from Finance:
1) Can we reduce the kickoff payment to 30% (instead of 40%)? That keeps our working capital lighter during the AP cutover.
2) We need the invoice VAT breakout and the exact reverse-charge wording you plan to use so our AP can code the invoices correctly.

If you can accept 30/60/10 (30% at Net30, 60% at Net45, 10% at Net60) we'll sign the payment addendum and return a signed PO. I've attached the signed PO for reference.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Liam

Attachments: signed_po_4571.pdf

--
Liam O'Connor
Head of Procurement, MediFlex Ltd.

Credit ops (Kimberly) — please run the 1–2 day credit review and temporarily raise the credit ceiling for PO_4571 to cover the Net60 exposure. If any concerns, flag to me and CC Legal.

Ops items:

- Billing: create invoice schedule in Zuora/Billing system with 3-line invoice plan (30%, 60%, 10%) and VAT reverse-charge note.
- CS: confirm delivery milestone definition so we can invoice the 60% at the correct event.
